scope: All non-deleted picture-based decks, including draft decks. HTTP availability and stored question-to-image associations; semantic image correctness requires content review.

questions.questionText: A patient undergoing evaluation for an unexplained immune-mediated disorder has serum tested using a multivalent antigen–antibody binding assay. The accompanying image shows multiple simultaneous interactions between a multivalent antibody and a multivalent antigen. Which immunologic concept is shown?

A patient with suspected immune complex–mediated pathology undergoes laboratory evaluation using an illustrated multivalent antigen–antibody lattice system. The image demonstrates multiple simultaneous interactions between antibody binding sites and multiple antigenic epitopes. Which immunologic concept is shown?

A patient is evaluated for autoimmune disease using Ouchterlony double immunodiffusion. The image shows precipitin lines from two antigen wells forming one continuous fused arc with the antibody well. Which immunologic reaction pattern is shown?

A patient with suspected mixed antigen exposure undergoes Ouchterlony testing. The image reveals two precipitin lines that cross each other without fusion. Which immunologic reaction pattern is shown?

A patient’s serum is examined using Ouchterlony immunodiffusion during evaluation of a suspected cross-reactive antibody. The photograph shows two antigen wells whose precipitin lines partially fuse but also form a characteristic spur. Which immunologic reaction pattern is shown?

A patient suspected of producing antibodies to two related antigens is tested using Ouchterlony diffusion. The image shows a fused precipitin line with a spur directed toward one antigen well. Which immunologic diffusion pattern is shown?

A patient undergoing antibody titration for transfusion evaluation produces a tube test result shown in the image: a homogeneously turbid suspension with no visible clumping. Which agglutination reading is shown?

A patient being screened for weak antibodies shows the reaction seen in the image: numerous microscopic granules, many free cells, and a dark, turbid supernate. Which agglutination reaction grade is shown?
A patient’s antibody screen yields an image demonstrating several large, distinct clumps with few free cells and a clear supernatant. Which reaction grade is shown?

A child presents with a mild febrile illness followed by a fine pink maculopapular rash that begins on the face and spreads downward. The image shows postauricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy. Which viral infection is shown?

A child presents with multiple superficial skin lesions that initially appeared as fragile vesicles and progressed to classic honey-colored crusts. The photograph now shows several older lesions that have darkened into thick, adherent crusts over shallow erosions. Which bacterial skin infection is shown?

A sexually active adult reports a single, firm, painless genital ulcer that developed gradually over several days. The photograph shows a clean-based, indurated lesion with sharply defined borders. Which sexually transmitted lesion is shown?

A patient presents with fever, malaise, and a diffuse rash. The image shows symmetric, copper-colored maculopapular lesions involving the trunk, extremities, palms, and soles. Which stage of Treponema pallidum infection is shown?

An adult with hyperviscosity symptoms undergoes serum protein electrophoresis. The image shows a very tall, narrow spike located between the β and γ regions. Which serum protein electrophoresis pattern is shown?

A patient with suspected connective tissue disease undergoes ANA testing. The image shows bright, diffuse fluorescence of the entire nucleus with no visible chromatin pattern and possible obscuration of nucleoli. Which ANA immunofluorescence pattern is shown?

A patient with systemic symptoms develops a facial rash. The photograph shows a red eruption over the cheeks and nasal bridge that distinctly spares the nasolabial folds. Which autoimmune manifestation is shown?

A patient evaluated for possible extractable nuclear antigen antibodies undergoes ANA testing. The image shows large, uneven fluorescent granules scattered throughout nuclei, with nonfluorescent nucleoli. Which ANA pattern is shown?

A patient suspected of systemic sclerosis undergoes ANA testing. The photograph shows intensely fluorescent, enlarged nucleoli with minimal surrounding nuclear staining. Which ANA immunofluorescence pattern is shown?

A patient with longstanding joint pain develops in the hands fixed deformities involving the MCP and PIP joints. The photograph shows marked ulnar deviation with symmetric involvement. Which rheumatologic condition is shown?

A 47-year-old patient undergoing evaluation for suspected infectious mononucleosis has serum tested by a manual agglutination assay. The photograph shows a reaction tube with markedly diminished agglutination despite clinical suspicion of a positive result. Repeat testing with serial dilutions produces strong agglutination at higher dilutions. Which serologic reaction pattern is shown?

A prenatal patient undergoing indirect antiglobulin testing shows no visible agglutination in the reaction tube, despite suspicion of the presence of IgG alloantibodies. Upon dilution of the serum, strong agglutination appears. The photograph shows the undiluted reaction with no agglutination. Which serologic reaction pattern is shown?

A recently transfused patient displays an unusual gel card pattern during antibody screening. The photograph reveals large agglutinated RBC clusters trapped in the upper gel matrix while a separate population of free red cells forms a pellet at the bottom. Which immunohematologic reaction pattern is shown?

A laboratory student is shown three unlabeled reagent bottles and three corresponding tubes prepared for ABO testing. Based on the photograph, Tube 2 shows the expected reaction pattern for anti-B testing. Which reagent bottle contains anti-B?

A patient undergoing pretransfusion testing has a reagent added during the antibody screen that reduces zeta potential and accelerates IgG binding to RBCs. The photograph shows the label of this potentiator. Which reagent is shown?

A donor blood specimen is typed using slide agglutination. The photograph shows strong agglutination with both anti-A and anti-B but no agglutination with anti-D. What is the blood type of the patient?

A patient undergoing emergency typing via gel card method shows no reaction in the anti-A and anti-B wells but clear agglutination in the anti-D well. The photograph confirms this pattern. Identify the blood type of the patient.
Which component of the chain of infection is enclosed in the box, characterized by the link connecting an infectious agent to a susceptible host through a defined route?
Which laboratory safety symbol is shown, characterized by three interlocking crescents surrounding a central circle to indicate materials capable of causing infection?
Which hazard symbol is shown, identified by a skull with crossed long bones beneath it to warn of substances capable of causing acute toxicity or death?
Which NFPA hazard component is shown, identified by the blue quadrant of the NFPA 704 diamond that expresses the degree of danger related to physiological impairment or biological harm?
Which urinalysis instrument is shown, identified by a weighted glass float submerged in urine to determine specific gravity based on its calibrated stem reading?
Which urinalysis instrument is shown, identified by its prism-based optical system requiring placement of a urine drop on a glass plate to measure specific gravity?

Which urinary sediment element is shown, identified by smooth, biconcave, non-nucleated discs appearing yellowish to faintly refractile under brightfield microscopy without significant morphological distortion?
Which urinary sediment element is shown, identified by round to oval refractile structures displaying budding forms that help differentiate them from similarly sized erythrocytes?

Which urinary sediment element is shown, identified by highly refractile spherical bodies that mimic erythrocytes but appear alongside large, flat squamous epithelial cells in KOVA-stained preparations?
Which urinary sediment artifact is shown, identified by a perfectly round, highly refractile sphere with a sharply defined outer margin that often mimics erythrocytes under brightfield microscopy?

A patient with hypotonic urine due to excessive water intake undergoes microscopic evaluation of urinary sediment. The photograph shows neutrophils with cytoplasm filled with highly refractile granules exhibiting active Brownian motion, creating a distinctive sparkling effect. Which urinary sediment element is shown?

A midstream urine specimen from a female patient is examined, and the photograph shows very large, flat, polygonal cells with small eccentric nuclei easily visible under low-power magnification. Which urinary sediment element is shown?

A patient with suspected lower urinary tract infection undergoes microscopic evaluation. The image reveals variably shaped cells—round, pear-shaped, or caudate—with centrally located nuclei and moderate cytoplasm. These cells appear to originate from the renal pelvis or bladder. Which urinary sediment element is shown?

A patient evaluated for urinary tract inflammation provides a urine sample, and the photograph demonstrates urothelial cells with irregular outlines and a distinctive tail-like cytoplasmic extension, giving a caudate form. The nuclei are centrally located. Which urinary sediment element is shown?

A patient suspected of acute tubular injury submits a urine sample. Microscopy shows small to medium oval cells with dense granular cytoplasm and eccentrically positioned nuclei consistent with distal tubular origin. Which urinary sediment element is shown?

A patient with nephrotic-range proteinuria undergoes urine microscopy. The photograph shows a cell containing abundant lipid droplets that display Maltese cross birefringence under polarized light. Which urinary sediment element is shown?

A patient evaluated for intravascular hemolysis undergoes urinary sediment staining. The photograph shows coarse intracellular granules staining deep blue with Prussian blue, indicating iron-laden macrophages. Which urinary sediment finding is shown?

A patient with recurrent urinary discomfort submits a urine sample. Microscopy reveals long, wavy, delicate strands lacking cellular borders and showing very low refractility, forming tangled ribbon-like structures. Which urinary sediment structure is shown?

A patient with suspected volume depletion undergoes urinalysis. The photograph shows colorless, homogeneous, cylindrical structures with smooth, parallel sides that are difficult to visualize due to their low refractility and are best appreciated under low-power magnification. Which urinary sediment structure is shown?

A patient presenting with cola-colored urine undergoes microscopy. The photograph shows a cylindrical cast densely packed with intact red blood cells, giving it a reddish-brown appearance. Which urinary sediment structure is shown?
Which urinary sediment structure is shown?
Which urinary sediment structure is shown, identified by a cylindrical Tamm–Horsfall protein matrix densely packed with nucleated epithelial cells originating from damaged renal tubules?
Which urinary crystal type is shown, identified by yellow-brown, fine, sand-like granules that form dense, amorphous clusters and typically appear in acidic urine?
Which urinary crystal type is shown, identified by colorless, highly refractile, envelope-shaped structures with a characteristic X-shaped central cross when viewed under high power?

Which urinary crystal type is shown, identified by colorless, highly refractile forms appearing as oval, dumbbell, or picket-fence shapes rather than the classic envelope morphology of their dihydrate counterpart?
Which urinary crystal type is shown, identified by large, colorless, highly refractile structures with a characteristic “coffin-lid” rectangular prism morphology?
Which urinary crystal type is shown, identified by colorless to white, fine, sand-like granules forming dense, amorphous clusters typically observed in alkaline urine such as pH 7.0?
Which urinary crystal type is shown, identified by yellow-brown, spherical bodies covered with irregular spicules that produce a characteristic “thorny apple” morphology?

Which urinary crystal type is shown, identified by colorless, highly refractile, perfectly flat, hexagonal plates that occur in acidic urine and strongly suggest an inherited amino acid transport defect?

A 6-year-old child with fulminant hepatic failure presents with dark urine and altered mental status. Urinalysis microscopy shows the crystalline structures in the photograph: colorless to yellow, highly refractile, fine needle-like crystals arranged in tight sheaves and radial clumps. Which urinary crystal type is shown?

An adult with nephrotic syndrome and heavy proteinuria undergoes urinalysis. The microscopic image shows large, flat, transparent plates with sharply defined, highly refractile borders and a characteristic notch at one or more corners. Which urinary crystal type is shown?

A patient with advanced chronic liver disease presents with dark urine. Microscopic examination of the urine shows yellow-brown, highly refractile, spherical crystals with prominent concentric rings and radial striations resembling an oily cross-section, as seen in the photograph. Which urinary crystal type is shown?

A jaundiced patient with marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia provides a urine sample for evaluation. The microscopic image reveals bright yellow to yellow-brown needle-like and granular pigment aggregates scattered throughout the field. Which urinary crystal type is shown?

A hospitalized patient receiving high-dose intravenous β-lactam therapy with ampicillin has a refrigerated urine specimen submitted for microscopy. The image shows long, thin, colorless needles arranged in dense, shock-like bundles throughout the field. Which urinary crystal type is shown?

A midstream urine specimen from an asymptomatic adult shows, on microscopy, a large, spherical, highly refractile structure with a thick outer wall and prominent internal concentric rings, as demonstrated in the photograph. The patient denies urinary symptoms, and the finding is suspected to be extraneous. Which urinary artifact is shown?

A urine specimen from a patient collected in a non-sterile container is examined microscopically. The image shows a long, straight to slightly twisted, highly refractile, thread-like structure lying beside a large squamous epithelial cell. Which urinary artifact is shown?

A urine specimen collected using powdered gloves is examined microscopically. The photograph shows round to oval, highly refractile bodies with a characteristic central dimple, some of which demonstrate a Maltese cross pattern under polarized light and may be mistaken for RBCs. Which urinary artifact is shown?

A patient with dark-colored urine, abdominal pain, and neurologic symptoms undergoes screening for porphyria. The Watson–Schwartz test is performed, and the red chromogen formed with Ehrlich’s reagent remains in the aqueous layer after sequential extraction with chloroform and n-butanol, as demonstrated in the reaction tubes shown. Which biochemical testing outcome is shown?

A patient undergoing lumbar puncture for evaluation of headache and suspected meningitis has CSF collected into four sequentially labeled tubes. When the tubes are held against a white background, the photograph shows Tube 1 as crystal-clear and water-like, while Tubes 2, 3, and 4 appear xanthochromic, hemolyzed, and cloudy, respectively. Which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) collection tube contains the normal specimen?

A 32-year-old man undergoing evaluation for infertility provides a semen sample for routine morphology assessment. The photomicrograph shows a spermatozoon with a prominent cap-like structure covering the anterior portion of the nucleus. Which component of the spermatozoon is shown?

A semen specimen from a 29-year-old male complaining of primary infertility is evaluated under high-power magnification. The spermatozoon shown in the photograph displays two fully formed heads attached to a single tail. Which interpretation best describes the spermatozoon shown?

A child with chronic diarrhea and suspected malabsorption undergoes fecal fat analysis. A Sudan III–stained preparation shows multiple intensely orange-red, round, highly refractile globules scattered throughout the field, as seen in the photograph. Which fecal element is shown?

A 32-year-old laboratory intern is reviewing equipment in the clinical chemistry section when she encounters the glass pipette shown in the photograph. It has a long, narrow body with graduation marks that stop before the tip. The supervising technologist reminds her that this pipette must be allowed to drain by gravity and should never be blown out. Which laboratory pipette is shown?

A biochemistry resident preparing enzyme standards inspects the pipette shown in the photograph. It has a bulb-shaped midsection and a single etched calibration mark, indicating that it is designed to deliver one exact, highly accurate volume. The resident notes that this type is commonly used for viscous biological fluids. Which laboratory pipette is shown?

A first-year medical technologist intern is shown the instrument in the photograph while learning basic liquid-handling techniques. The device is made of a single piece of flexible plastic with an integrated bulb and an ungraduated stem used only for approximate fluid transfer. Which laboratory device is shown?

A quality control officer is shown the weighing instrument in the photograph while conducting routine equipment verification. The device features an enclosed chamber surrounding the weighing pan and displays measurements to 0.1 mg or better. Which laboratory instrument is shown?

A clinical laboratory trainee examines the instrument shown in the photograph while preparing to process blood specimens. The device is a compact, enclosed unit that sits on the benchtop and contains a rotor capable of spinning tubes at controlled speeds for density-based separation. Which laboratory instrument is shown?

A laboratory scientist reviews the centrifuge rotor shown in the photograph. The rotor consists of buckets that hang vertically at rest but pivot outward to become horizontal during spinning, ensuring uniform sedimentation. Which laboratory instrument is shown?
A safety officer trains new staff using the pictogram shown in the photograph, which displays a human torso with an exploding star-like symbol at the chest. Which safety symbol is shown?

A fire-safety orientation includes the pictogram shown in the photograph. It consists of a stylized flame inside a red diamond, indicating substances that readily ignite. Which safety symbol is shown?

A clinical chemist reviews the analytical concept illustrated in the photograph showing repeated measurements producing varying but closely clustered results. The evaluation focuses on the closeness of replicate results to one another, not to the true value. Which analytical concept is shown?

A method-validation specialist reviews the graph shown in the photograph, which displays bias assessment through recovery studies, interference testing, and comparison-of-methods analysis to determine deviation from the true value. Which analytical concept is shown?

A researcher calibrating a new spectrophotometric detection system examines the component shown in the photograph. The boxed structure contains a sealed vacuum tube with a photocathode and multiple dynodes arranged to amplify electrons released by incident photons, allowing detection of extremely low light levels. Which spectrophotometer component is shown?

A clinical laboratory scientist investigating a sample’s fluorescence places a cuvette into the instrument shown in the photograph. The setup includes an excitation light source, an excitation monochromator, a cuvette holder, and an emission detector arranged at a 90° angle to the incoming excitation beam. Which analytical instrument is shown?

A biochemist reviewing core biomolecules examines the structure shown in the photograph. The molecule contains a central α-carbon bonded to an amino group, a carboxyl group, a hydrogen atom, and a variable side chain. Which biochemical classification is shown?

A 54-year-old patient with generalized edema undergoes serum protein electrophoresis. The photograph of the electrophoretic pattern shows markedly reduced albumin, an elevated α₂-globulin fraction, and increased β-lipoprotein presence. Which electrophoretic pattern is shown?

A febrile patient suspected of infection undergoes serum protein electrophoresis. The photograph shows elevated α₁- and α₂-globulin fractions with a slight reduction in albumin. Which serum protein electrophoretic pattern is shown?

A 38-year-old patient with early-onset emphysema has serum protein electrophoresis performed. The photograph reveals a markedly diminished α₁-globulin band. Which serum protein electrophoretic pattern is shown?

A patient with recurrent infections undergoes serum protein electrophoresis. The photograph shows a significantly decreased γ-globulin region with preservation of other fractions. Which serum protein electrophoretic pattern is shown?

A patient being evaluated for plasma cell dyscrasia undergoes serum protein electrophoresis. The photograph demonstrates a narrow, tall spike in the γ-region. Which serum protein electrophoretic pattern is shown?
A patient with chronic liver disease undergoes serum protein electrophoresis. The photograph shows a wide, diffuse elevation of the γ-region. Which serum protein electrophoretic pattern is shown?

A patient with advanced hepatic failure has serum protein electrophoresis performed. The photograph shows markedly decreased albumin, reduced α- and β-fractions, and possible β–γ bridging. Which serum protein electrophoretic pattern is shown?

A 62-year-old man with long-standing alcohol use disorder presents for evaluation of progressive abdominal distention and scleral icterus. Serum protein electrophoresis is performed, and the photograph shows a characteristic fusion of the β- and γ-regions, with decreased albumin. Which serum protein electrophoretic pattern is shown?

A 45-year-old woman undergoes neck imaging for evaluation of a painless anterior neck mass. The photograph of the excised specimen shows a bilobed structure connected by a narrow isthmus. Histologic sections reveal numerous spherical follicles filled with eosinophilic colloid. Which organ is shown?
Which bacterium is shown, identified by its smooth, round, pink colonies on MacConkey agar indicating strong lactose fermentation?
Which bacterium is shown, identified by its colorless, non–lactose-fermenting colonies with a characteristic rough surface appearance on MacConkey agar?
Which bacterial group is shown, identified by its purple coloration after Gram staining due to retention of crystal violet within a thick peptidoglycan layer?
Which bacterial group is shown, identified by its pink to reddish appearance after Gram staining due to decolorization and uptake of the safranin counterstain?
Which staining result is shown, identified by the presence of bright red rods that retain carbol fuchsin after acid-alcohol decolorization in the Ziehl–Neelsen method?
Which organism is shown, identified by its smooth, purple-tinted to whitish colonies that grow only on buffered charcoal–yeast extract (BCYE) enrichment medium?
Which bacterial reaction is shown, identified by the deep purple colonies at arrow A compared with the light pink to colorless colonies at arrow B on MacConkey agar?
Which hemolysis pattern is shown?
Which result is shown, identified by the presence of a clear zone of growth inhibition around the vancomycin disk for one organism but not the other?

A clinical microbiology technologist examines a disk diffusion plate from a patient with a complicated urinary tract infection. When the plate is viewed with light passing upward through the agar, the photograph clearly shows sharply defined inhibition zone edges. Which lighting method is shown?

A 54-year-old patient on long-term antibiotic therapy submits a wound culture for susceptibility testing. The disk diffusion plate in the photograph shows discrete bacterial colonies growing within the cleared inhibition zone surrounding an antimicrobial disk. Which phenomenon is shown?

A 38-year-old patient with recurrent sinusitis undergoes culture testing, and the laboratory photograph shows a plastic strip on an agar plate generating an elliptical inhibition pattern. The MIC is read at the point where the ellipse meets the numeric scale on the strip. Which antimicrobial testing method is shown?

A 71-year-old patient receiving ampicillin is tested for beta-lactamase production. The photograph of a chromogenic cephalosporin disk shows a deep pink color developing on the left. Which result is shown on the left?

A respiratory isolate from a patient with suspected Pseudomonas infection is tested using the acetamide utilization assay. The photograph shows the left tube turning blue, while the right tube remains unchanged in color. Which result is shown in the right tube?

A stool isolate is evaluated for group D Enterococcus using the bile esculin test. The photograph shows the left tube turning black while the right tube remains unchanged. Which result is shown on the left?
A clinical isolate from a wound infection is tested with hydrogen peroxide. The photograph shows vigorous bubbling immediately after reagent application. Which biochemical test is shown?

A blood culture isolate suspected to be Staphylococcus aureus is evaluated with a plasma-containing tube. The photograph shows clot formation in the tube on the left, while the right tube remains liquid. Which reaction is shown?

A decarboxylase test panel is examined for ornithine decarboxylase activity in an Enterobacteriaceae isolate. The photograph shows tube A turning purple, tube B turning yellow, and tube C remaining unchanged with no turbidity. Which tube is shown?

A wound isolate is evaluated for gelatinase using nutrient gelatin medium. After refrigeration, the photograph shows the left tube remaining liquefied while the right tube is solid. Which biochemical test is shown?
Which organism is shown, identified by its ability to grow at an elevated incubation temperature of 42 °C?
Which biochemical test is shown, identified by the development of a red layer after addition of Kovac’s reagent to detect tryptophan degradation?
Which biochemical test is shown, identified by its ability to detect lysine decarboxylation, lysine deamination, glucose fermentation, and hydrogen sulfide production in a single differential medium?
Which tube shows negative motility?
Which tube is the oxidizer?
Which tube represents the typical triple sugar iron agar reaction of Edwardsiella?

Which organism is shown, identified by its growth up to the bacitracin (Taxo A) disk indicating resistance, along with a clear zone of inhibition around the furazolidone (FX) disk indicating susceptibility?
Which bacterial morphology is shown, identified by spherical cells arranged in long, bead-like chains on Gram stain?
Which organism is shown, identified by its nonhemolytic, ground-glass colonies with characteristic filamentous edges that produce a “comet tail” or Medusa-head appearance on sheep blood agar?
Which condition is shown, identified by the painless black eschar with surrounding edema characteristic of infection by a spore-forming Gram-positive bacillus?

A 5-year-old unimmunized child presents with sore throat, low-grade fever, and a grayish pharyngeal membrane. A Gram stain of a throat swab, as shown in the photograph, reveals pleomorphic, club-shaped Gram-positive rods arranged in palisades and angular “Chinese-letter” formations. Which organism is shown?

A patient with suspected diphtheria has a throat swab cultured on Tinsdale agar. The plate, shown in the photograph, demonstrates black colonies surrounded by a distinct brown halo. Which organism is shown?

A 29-year-old pregnant woman develops fever and flu-like symptoms. A Gram-positive rod is isolated from blood culture and inoculated into semisolid motility medium. After incubation at room temperature, the photograph shows a characteristic umbrella-shaped zone of sub-surface growth. Which organism is shown?

A 55-year-old man receiving long-term corticosteroid therapy presents with chronic pulmonary symptoms. A culture on chocolate agar, shown in the photograph, reveals dry, chalky, wrinkled colonies with an earthy odor. Microscopy demonstrates branching, filamentous Gram-positive bacilli that are partially acid-fast. Which organism is shown?

A neonate in the intensive care unit develops sepsis after being fed powdered formula. Blood culture grows a Gram-negative rod. On sheep blood agar, the photograph shows mucoid colonies; on EMB agar, the colonies appear pale and weakly lactose fermenting without a metallic sheen. Which organism is shown?

A 40-year-old hospitalized patient has a Gram-negative rod isolated from a catheter tip. The organism grows on MacConkey agar, and the photograph shows distinct red-pigmented colonies even on this selective medium. Which organism is shown?

A 6-year-old child with fever and abdominal pain has a stool culture planted on cefsulodin-irgasan-novobiocin (CIN) agar. The photograph shows colonies with a deep red center and a translucent peripheral halo, creating a “bull’s-eye” appearance. Which organism is shown?

A urine culture from a patient with recurrent urinary tract infections is plated on sheep blood agar. The photograph demonstrates broad, concentric waves of spreading growth that cover the entire plate, obliterating individual colonies. Which organism is shown?
A stool culture from a patient with acute diarrhea is grown on EMB agar. The photograph shows dark colonies with an intense green metallic sheen. Which organism is shown?

A 19-year-old patient with cystic fibrosis has a respiratory culture plated on selective media. The photograph shows markedly mucoid colonies with a glistening surface and a faint light blue hue. Which organism is shown?

A 62-year-old man with cystic fibrosis is admitted for worsening pneumonia. A respiratory culture is plated on chocolate agar, and the photograph shows smooth colonies producing a dull green discoloration without any blue-green fluorescence. Which organism is shown?

A 7-year-old boy from a tropical region presents with cellulitis after swimming in stagnant water. DNase agar culture, shown in the photograph, reveals intensely violet colonies. Which organism is shown?

A patient with suspected cholera has a stool sample cultured on TCBS agar. The photograph shows large, smooth, bright yellow colonies consistent with strong sucrose fermentation. Which organism is shown?

A stool culture from a patient with profuse watery diarrhea undergoes a sodium deoxycholate string test. When the colony is lifted, a long, mucoid DNA “string” forms, as shown in the photograph. Which organism is shown?

A 3-year-old child with epiglottitis undergoes a throat swab culture. The photograph shows tiny colonies growing only within the hemolytic zone around Staphylococcus aureus on blood agar. Which organism is shown?
A child with persistent cough undergoes nasopharyngeal culture on Regan–Lowe agar. The photograph shows small, shiny, pearl-like colonies resembling mercury droplets. Which organism is shown?

A genital specimen from a patient with suspected gonorrhea is inoculated onto modified Thayer–Martin medium and placed into a sealed pouch with a gas-generating tablet, as shown in the photograph. Which incubation system is depicted?
A wound specimen cultured anaerobically on blood agar shows colonies with a classic double zone of hemolysis, as seen in the photograph. Which organism is shown?
A hospitalized patient with antibiotic-associated diarrhea has a stool culture plated on CCFA. The photograph shows yellow, ground-glass, uneven colonies. Which organism is shown?

A 45-year-old man with periodontal disease has an anaerobic culture performed. The photograph shows irregular, crumb-like colonies with green discoloration of the agar beneath. Which organism is shown?

A 37-year-old aquarium maintenance worker presents with chronic nonhealing skin nodules on the hands and forearms after repeated minor abrasions from aquarium water. A Gram stain from a skin biopsy, shown in the photograph, reveals long, beaded, irregularly staining rods. Which organism is shown?

A 50-year-old immigrant with chronic cough and weight loss has a sputum culture placed on Löwenstein–Jensen medium. After several weeks, the photograph shows rough, dry, buff-colored colonies with a cauliflower-like texture. Which organism is shown?

A 27-year-old woman with a soft tissue infection has a culture plated onto Löwenstein–Jensen medium. Within a few days, the photograph shows smooth, creamy, multilobate colonies consistent with rapid growth. Which organism is shown?

A specimen from a patient with suspected tuberculosis undergoes biochemical testing. The photograph shows a filter paper strip turning yellow after application of an organism extract. Which test is shown?

A 22-year-old college student with atypical pneumonia has a throat culture incubated on specialized media. Under low-power magnification, the photograph shows minute colonies with a dense central zone and lighter peripheral ring, resembling a “fried egg.” Which organism is shown?

A penile chancre sample from a patient with suspected syphilis is examined using dark-field microscopy. The photograph shows thin, tightly coiled, corkscrew-shaped organisms exhibiting graceful flexion. Which organism is shown?

A 32-year-old hiker presents with fever and an enlarging skin lesion after a tick bite. The photograph shows a large, erythematous ring with central clearing forming a bull’s-eye pattern. Which condition is shown?

A stool specimen from a 34-year-old patient with intermittent diarrhea and recent travel history is examined under trichrome stain. The image shows a trophozoite with a single nucleus containing a small, centrally positioned karyosome and finely, evenly distributed peripheral chromatin forming a smooth, regular nuclear border. Which parasitic organism is shown?

A formed stool sample from a 27-year-old patient with abdominal cramping is examined using iron hematoxylin stain. The image shows a cyst-like structure containing a single nucleus and distinct, smooth, cigar-shaped chromatoid bars. Based on the morphology seen in the photo, which intestinal protozoan is most likely present?

A fresh stool specimen from a 39-year-old patient undergoing evaluation for chronic loose stools is stained with iron hematoxylin. The image shows a trophozoite displaying a broad pseudopod (indicated by the arrow), coarse and irregularly clumped peripheral chromatin, and an atypical or slightly eccentric karyosome that gives the nucleus an uneven, irregular outline. Which protozoan trophozoite is depicted?
Which protozoan trophozoite is shown, identified by its coarse peripheral chromatin, irregular nuclear outline, and generally sluggish motility?

A stool specimen from a 30-year-old patient undergoing evaluation for gastrointestinal discomfort is stained with trichrome. The image shows a spherical cyst containing five clearly visible nuclei. No chromatoid bodies with smooth ends are observed, and the cyst appears larger than typical small amoebic cysts. Based on the nuclear count and morphology, which intestinal cyst is shown?

A stool sample from a 25-year-old patient presenting with mild gastrointestinal discomfort is examined under trichrome stain. The image reveals a very small trophozoite with irregular, slightly jerky motility. The nucleus contains a large, blot-like karyosome with no visible peripheral chromatin. Based on the microscopic appearance shown, which protozoan trophozoite is present?

A stool specimen from a 22-year-old patient undergoing routine screening is stained with trichrome. The microscopic image shows a very small cyst containing four nuclei, each displaying a large, blot-like karyosome and an absence of peripheral chromatin. No glycogen vacuole or chromatoid bodies are visible. Based on the nuclear morphology and size, which intestinal cyst is shown?

A stool smear stained with trichrome shows large amoebic trophozoites with a single eccentric karyosome lacking peripheral chromatin. The cytoplasm appears granular and markedly vacuolated. Which protozoan trophozoites are shown?
A concentrated stool specimen shows a cyst with a single nucleus containing a large karyosome and a well-defined glycogen vacuole that stains prominently. Which intestinal cyst is shown?
A corneal scraping stained with iron hematoxylin reveals a free-living amoebic trophozoite possessing multiple thornlike projections (acanthopodia). Which organism is shown?

A brain biopsy stained with iron hematoxylin reveals round cysts with an irregular double wall and a cytoplasm filled with multiple vacuoles and disorganized internal material. Which free-living amoeba cyst is shown?

A trichrome-stained stool smear shows a bilaterally symmetrical trophozoite with a pear-shaped body and two centrally located nuclei staining bright red. Which intestinal protozoan trophozoite is shown?
A preserved stool specimen reveals an oval cyst with multiple nuclei staining intensely red on trichrome stain, along with internal fibrils suggestive of median bodies. Which cyst is shown?
A wet preparation of stool shows a motile, pear-shaped trophozoite with a single nucleus and a distinctive spiral cytostome along its anterior region. Which protozoan trophozoite is shown?

A concentrated stool sample reveals a lemon-shaped cyst with an anterior hyaline knob, a single nucleus, and a curved cytostomal fibril resembling a shepherd’s crook. Which intestinal protozoan cyst is shown?
A phase-contrast wet mount of vaginal discharge shows numerous motile, pear-shaped organisms demonstrating jerky, tumbling movement around squamous epithelial cells. Which protozoan is shown?
A bone marrow aspirate shows intracellular oval organisms within macrophages, each containing a nucleus and a rod-shaped kinetoplast, giving a dot-dash appearance. Which parasitic form is shown?

A peripheral blood smear stained with Giemsa shows an S-shaped extracellular hemoflagellate with a full-length undulating membrane and a prominent posterior kinetoplast. Which hemoflagellate is shown?
A febrile patient’s stained blood smear shows an extracellular protozoan with a classic C-shaped curvature and a long undulating membrane. Which hemoflagellate is shown?
A Giemsa-stained peripheral smear shows an enlarged RBC containing numerous merozoites and fine red stippling along the cell membrane known as Schüffner’s dots. Which malaria parasite stage is shown?
A Giemsa-stained blood smear from a patient with suspected malaria shows a crescent-shaped organism occupying an RBC. Which malaria parasite form is shown?
A stool wet mount shows a large, oval protozoan fully covered with cilia and possessing a distinct oral groove along one side. Which intestinal protozoan trophozoite is shown?
A concentrated stool sample reveals a large, spherical cyst with a thick wall and internal remnants of cilia. Which intestinal protozoan cyst is shown?

A modified acid-fast stained stool smear shows numerous round, bright pink oocysts measuring 4–6 µm, each with internal granules representing developing sporozoites. Which intestinal parasite is shown?

A trichrome-stained stool specimen shows a round organism with a large central vacuole pushing multiple nuclei to the periphery, giving a characteristic halo-like appearance. Which intestinal protozoan is shown?
A lung biopsy stained with iron hematoxylin shows clusters of rounded, cyst-like structures with crescentic internal forms resembling crushed ping-pong balls. Which opportunistic pathogen is shown?
A cellophane tape preparation shows elongated, ovoid helminth eggs with one flattened side and a fully formed larva inside. Which helminth egg is shown?

A stool specimen from a 7-year-old child with chronic diarrhea is examined under the microscope. The image shows a brown, barrel-shaped helminth egg with a thick shell and very prominent bipolar plugs at each end. Which helminth egg is shown?
Which helminth egg is shown in the stool specimen, appearing elongated and irregular with disorganized internal contents and lacking the typical thick, mammillated outer coat?

A direct smear of a stool sample from a patient with suspected ascariasis shows large, oval eggs with a thick, coarsely mammillated outer shell and a developing embryo inside. Which helminth is identified by this egg morphology?

During a community deworming program, a large intestinal worm passed in stool is submitted for identification. The specimen is a cream-colored, cylindrical helminth with smooth cuticle and tapered ends, consistent with an adult female roundworm. Which helminth is shown?

A fresh stool specimen from a patient with iron-deficiency anemia is examined, and the microscopic image shows thin-shelled, oval eggs containing a segmenting embryo (morula-like appearance). Which helminth egg is shown?

A stool culture incubated for several hours is examined, and a rhabditiform larva is seen on the slide. The larva has a long buccal cavity and a relatively inconspicuous genital primordium. Which helminth is shown?

A stool sample from an immunocompromised patient is examined, and a rhabditiform larva is observed under the microscope. The image shows a short buccal cavity and a very prominent genital primordium. Which larval form is shown?

A muscle biopsy from a patient presenting with myalgia and eosinophilia is examined histologically. The image reveals coiled larvae encysted within striated skeletal muscle fibers, each larva enclosed in a nurse cell-like structure. Which parasite is shown?

A nocturnal blood sample stained with Giemsa is examined under the microscope. The image shows a sheathed microfilaria with a clear space at the tip of the tail where nuclei are absent. Which microfilaria is shown?
A stained peripheral blood smear from a patient in an endemic area shows a sheathed microfilaria whose tail contains distinct terminal nuclei at the tip. Which microfilaria is shown?

A skin snip preparation from a patient living near fast-flowing rivers shows an unsheathed microfilaria with nuclei that are scattered throughout the body but do not extend to the tip of the tail. Which microfilaria is shown?
A fecal flotation specimen shows a round to oval helminth egg with a thick, radially striated outer shell and a clearly visible hexacanth embryo containing six hooklets. Which helminth egg is shown?
A proglottid sample reveals an armed scolex with four muscular suckers and a rostellum bearing a double row of hooklets. Which organism is shown?
A stool specimen shows a small, oval egg with a thin hyaline shell, distinct polar thickenings, and polar filaments extending into the space between the shell and embryo. Which helminth egg is shown?
A pet-owner’s stool sample shows an egg packet: multiple hexacanth embryos enclosed within a single thin-walled capsule. Which helminth is shown?
A fecal specimen reveals an oval, yellow-brown egg with a distinct operculum at one pole and a small terminal knob at the opposite end. Which helminth egg is shown?
A stool sample reveals a small operculated egg with pronounced opercular shoulders and a tiny abopercular knob. Which helminth egg is shown?
A sputum specimen from a patient with chronic cough shows a golden-brown, asymmetrical, operculated egg with a thick shell and prominent shoulders. Which helminth egg is shown?
A fresh stool exam shows an elongated, oval egg with a prominent lateral spine extending from one side of the shell. Which helminth egg is shown?
A liver biopsy shows small, rounded schistosome eggs with a subtle, almost imperceptible lateral spine. Which helminth egg is shown?

A 25-year-old male from an endemic region presents with painless terminal hematuria. A urine sample collected around midday is concentrated and examined microscopically. The image shows an elongated, golden-brown egg with a prominent, sharply pointed spine at one end. Which helminth egg is shown?

A stool wet mount from a patient with chronic diarrhea is examined under saline. The image shows multiple round, variably sized, highly refractile spheres that float toward the edge of the coverslip and lack any visible shells, embryos, or internal structures. Which structure is shown?

A stool specimen prepared in saline is examined under high power. The photomicrograph shows a long, twisted, refractile, helical ribbon-like structure, consistent with plant cellulose, with no shell, operculum, or internal embryonic content. Which structure is shown?

A skin scraping taken from the burrow lesions of a patient with intense nocturnal pruritus is examined in saline. The image shows a round to globular mite with a thick body, short stubby legs that do not extend beyond the body margin, and a compact, burrowing morphology. Which organism is shown?

A saline skin scraping from the same pruritic patient is examined under high power. The image shows smooth, oval, thin-shelled structures containing homogeneous internal material, without operculum, terminal knob, or polar plugs. These are seen adjacent to adult mites. Which structure is shown?

A patient in a crowded shelter presents with intense pruritus and visible insects in clothing seams. A saline mount of material from the clothing is examined. The image shows an elongated, dorsoventrally flattened insect with a segmented abdomen and six legs ending in strong claws. Which organism is shown?

A technologist demonstrates the formalin–ethyl acetate concentration technique. After centrifugation, the tube is photographed. Four distinct layers can be seen from bottom to top: sediment, a clear liquid layer, a dark debris plug, and an upper solvent layer. In the image, which layer is the second from the bottom?

At autopsy, brain tissue from a previously healthy child who died after a rapidly progressive meningoencephalitis is examined with hematoxylin and eosin stain. The photomicrograph shows large amoeboid trophozoites with a prominent central karyosome invading the brain parenchyma with acute inflammatory changes. Which organism is shown?

A muscle biopsy from a patient with myalgia, eosinophilia, and a history of eating undercooked pork is examined histologically. The image shows coiled larvae enclosed within thick-walled capsules embedded in striated skeletal muscle fibers. Which helminth stage is shown?

A blood-sucking arthropod recovered from a rodent-infested dwelling is examined at 400× magnification. The image shows a laterally compressed body, strong jumping hind legs, and absence of both genal and pronotal combs. Which arthropod is shown?

A stool specimen from an asymptomatic adult undergoing routine screening is examined with iodine wet mount. The photomicrograph shows a small (≤10 µm), oval cyst with up to four nuclei, resembling Entamoeba but clearly smaller than typical E. histolytica. No distinct peripheral chromatin is seen, and no glycogen vacuole is present. Which intestinal protozoan cyst is shown?

A stool sample from a camper with steatorrhea and foul-smelling diarrhea is stained with trichrome. The image shows a pear-shaped trophozoite with a dorsoventrally flattened body, bilaterally symmetrical “face-like” appearance, and two prominent nuclei resembling eyes. Which protozoan trophozoite is shown?

A concentrated stool specimen from a traveler with intermittent diarrhea is examined by trichrome stain. The photomicrograph shows an oval, thick-walled cyst with internal fibrils and up to four nuclei arranged in pairs along a longitudinal median axis, giving a bilaterally symmetrical appearance. Which protozoan cyst is shown?

A modified acid-fast–stained stool smear from an immunocompetent hiker with prolonged watery diarrhea is examined. The image shows spherical oocysts approximately 8–10 µm in diameter that exhibit bright blue-green autofluorescence under UV illumination. Which intestinal coccidian is shown?

A peripheral blood smear from a patient with chronic low-grade fever and splenomegaly is examined. The photomicrograph shows an enlarged but not grossly distorted RBC containing a compact schizont with 6–12 merozoites arranged in a classic “rosette” or daisy-head pattern. Which intraerythrocytic parasite stage is shown?

A Giemsa-stained blood smear from a febrile patient returning from Southeast Asia shows round-to-oval intraerythrocytic microgametocytes with dense chromatin and pale blue cytoplasm within normocytic, non-enlarged RBCs. The overall morphology resembles P. malariae, but the clinical course has been rapidly progressive with daily (quotidian) fevers. Which Plasmodium species is shown?

A thin blood smear from a splenectomized patient with hemolytic anemia and fever is examined. The image shows pleomorphic intraerythrocytic ring forms, some in pairs, without visible hemozoin pigment, and a few erythrocytes contain tetrad formations resembling a Maltese cross. Which intraerythrocytic organism is shown?

A young contact lens wearer presents with severe ocular pain, photophobia, and blurred vision. Corneal scraping and slit-lamp examination reveal a classic ring-shaped stromal infiltrate with radial perineural extension consistent with keratoneuritis. Which pathogen causes the disease shown?

A 29-year-old woman presents with vaginal discharge and itching. A Papanicolaou smear is examined, and the photomicrograph shows a pear-shaped protozoan with pale granular cytoplasm, an eccentrically placed nucleus, and faint outlines of an undulating membrane and flagella. Which protozoan is shown?

A brain biopsy from a patient with seizures and chorioretinitis is examined histologically. The photomicrograph shows a rounded tissue cyst located in neural tissue, filled with numerous crescentic bradyzoites packed tightly within a well-defined cyst wall. Similar cysts are also reported in muscle and ocular tissue. Which protozoan structure is shown?

A stool specimen from a child with poor hygiene is examined by wet mount and concentration technique. The image reveals large, brownish ova with a thick, mammillated albuminous coat; another similar egg in the same field appears smooth, lacking the rough outer layer but retaining a thick shell. Which helminth egg is shown?

During a mass deworming campaign, a large intestinal roundworm passed in stool is submitted to the laboratory. The image of the adult nematode shows a long, cylindrical body with a distinctly ventrally curved posterior end, consistent with a male worm. Which nematode is shown?

A perianal tape preparation from a child with nocturnal pruritus is examined. The photomicrograph shows a long, slender nematode, tapering at both ends, with the body cavity filled with numerous planoconvex eggs visible through the cuticle. Which nematode is shown?

A stool specimen from a farmer with abdominal discomfort is examined. The photomicrograph shows an elongated, thin-shelled egg containing a morula, resembling a hookworm egg but noticeably larger and more tapered at the poles. Which helminth egg is shown?

A colonoscopy specimen from a patient with chronic abdominal pain reveals thin, thread-like worms embedded in the cecal mucosa. The image shows adults with a long, slender anterior filament and a thicker posterior body, giving a whip-like appearance. Which nematode is shown?

A fresh stool sample from a patient with suspected hookworm infection is cultured and examined. The image shows a rhabditiform larva with a long buccal cavity and an inconspicuous genital primordium, consistent with early development in feces. Which larval nematode is shown?

A soil sample from a playground frequented by dogs is examined for zoonotic parasites. The photomicrograph shows a thick-shelled, nearly spherical egg with a coarsely pitted outer surface and a developing infectious L2 larva inside. Which helminth egg is shown?

A resident in a rural village presents with a painful blister on the lower leg. On immersion of the affected limb in water, a long, white, thread-like worm is observed emerging from the skin lesion. The photograph captures the adult female worm protruding through the blister. Which parasite is shown?

A 6-year-old child with a history of close contact with household pets passes tapeworm segments in the stool. On gross inspection and in the provided image, the proglottids are elongate and barrel-shaped, often compared to cucumber seeds. Which cestode is shown?

A stool specimen from a patient with suspected taeniasis is examined with iodine wet mount. The image shows a round to slightly oval egg with a thick outer wall displaying prominent radial striations (embryophore) surrounding a central oncosphere. Which helminth egg is shown?

A fecal sample from a rodent-infested storage area is examined. The image reveals a single, thick-shelled, round egg with a smooth outer surface enclosing a central oncosphere with six hooklets, and no polar filaments are seen. Which cestode egg is shown?

A surgically removed liver cyst from a shepherd is aspirated, and the sediment is examined microscopically. The image shows numerous free-floating protoscolices (hydatid sand) and refractile hooklets within a fluid-filled cyst cavity. Which cestode structure is shown?

A 32-year-old farmer from a rural endemic area undergoes endoscopy for chronic diarrhea and malabsorption. The photograph of the intestinal lumen reveals a very large, fleshy, leaf-shaped trematode attached to the mucosa, lacking any cephalic cone or distinct anterior projection. Which trematode is shown?

Stool from a patient with suspected hepatobiliary fluke infection is examined. The image shows a large, ellipsoidal, yellow-brown operculated egg measuring about 130–150 µm, morphologically indistinguishable from eggs produced by the giant intestinal fluke. Which trematode egg is shown?

A biliary tract specimen from a patient with recurrent cholangitis is examined. The image shows a small, elongated, spatulate trematode with a tapered anterior end and a more rounded posterior. Internally, two highly branched, dendritic testes are located in the posterior third of the body. Which trematode is shown?

A stool specimen from a patient with chronic schistosomiasis is examined. The image shows a rounded to ovoid egg with a small, subtle lateral knob that is barely perceptible, without a prominent terminal or large lateral spine. Which helminth egg is shown?

A patient with chronic sinus colonization is evaluated for a suspected opportunistic mold infection. The photo shows delicate hyphae with simple conidiophores producing solitary to clustered oval conidia. Which fungal structure is shown?

A bronchoalveolar lavage culture from a patient with near-drowning exposure shows annellated conidiophores bearing solitary smooth oval conidia. The image displays the classic asexual structure. Which fungal organism is shown?

A rapidly progressing sinus infection in an immunocompromised patient shows broad, ribbon-like hyphae terminating in large spherical structures filled with spores. The image confirms these enclosed sporangiospores. Which fungal group is shown?

A nasal necrotic lesion smear shows broad aseptate hyphae with spherical sporangia but no rhizoids at the sporangiophore base. The image highlights the absence of rhizoids. Which fungal organism is shown?
A bone marrow aspirate from a patient with cave exposure shows numerous tiny intracellular yeasts (2–5 μm) fluorescing under calcofluor white stain within macrophages. Which fungal pathogen is shown?

A skin scraping culture from a tinea corporis lesion shows hyphae with numerous tear-shaped microconidia borne singly along the hyphae. No grape-like clusters or spiral hyphae are present. Which dermatophyte is shown?
A scalp scraping from a patient with chronic tinea favosa shows swollen, antler-like hyphal tips forming favic chandeliers with no conidia present on the photomicrograph. Which dermatophyte is shown?

A hair culture shows abundant large rough-walled spindle-shaped macroconidia with thick walls and sharply pointed ends. The image emphasizes these elongated echinulate structures. Which dermatophyte is shown?

A soil-associated dermatophyte culture shows abundant ellipsoidal macroconidia with moderately rough walls, rounded ends, and 4–6 cells. The image highlights their symmetrical shape. Which dermatophyte is shown?

A culture from tinea cruris displays numerous smooth, thin-walled, multiseptate club-shaped macroconidia with absence of microconidia. The image shows only these large club-shaped structures. Which dermatophyte is shown?

A patient with chronic pulmonary symptoms undergoes sputum cytology, and the Papanicolaou-stained smear shows slender, septate hyphae branching dichotomously at acute angles, as seen in the photo. Which mold is shown?

A respiratory culture from an immunocompromised patient shows a smooth, short conidiophore terminating in a compact, columnar conidial head arising from a uniseriate phialide arrangement on the upper portion of a small vesicle, as seen in the photo. Which mold is shown?

A culture from a patient with allergic bronchopulmonary symptoms shows a large spherical vesicle with biseriate phialides (metulae and phialides) producing dense, radiating chains of dark conidia, as demonstrated in the photo. Which mold is shown?
A culture from a keratitis case shows numerous multicelled, sickle-shaped macroconidia with thin walls, multiple septa, and pointed ends, as seen in the photomicrograph. Which mold is shown?

A culture isolated from oral lesions shows true hyphae fragmenting into rectangular arthroconidia that are directly adjacent without intervening empty spaces, as shown in the photo. Which fungal organism is shown?
A mold isolated from deteriorating fruit shows classic brushlike conidiophores (penicilli) composed of branched phialides producing chains of round conidia, as pictured. Which mold is shown?

A patient from an endemic region presents with cutaneous lesions, and the tissue section shows large thick-walled yeast cells exhibiting broad-based budding, as seen in the photo. Which fungal organism is shown?
A biopsy from a necrotic lung lesion shows a thick-walled spherule filled with numerous small internal endospores, as shown in the image. Which fungal pathogen is shown?
A mold culture shows alternating thick-walled barrel-shaped arthroconidia separated by empty disjunctor cells, as highlighted in the photo. Which fungal organism is shown?
A bone marrow sample shows numerous tiny, uniform, oval yeasts measuring 2–5 µm, many clustered intracellularly within macrophages, as seen in the photo. Which fungal organism is shown?

A skin biopsy culture from a patient with chronic respiratory symptoms shows thin, branching hyphae bearing single, oval conidia attached laterally along the hyphal surface, as seen in the photo. Which mold is shown in its mycelial phase?

A respiratory culture from a patient with chronic pulmonary disease reveals large, thick-walled, round macroconidia covered with prominent spike-like tuberculations, as seen in the photomicrograph. Which mold is shown in its mycelial phase?

A biopsy from a subcutaneous nodule shows darkly pigmented hyphae with a long, slender annellophore tapering to a narrow tip that produces slim, discrete annelloconidia, as shown in the image. Which mold is shown?

A bronchoalveolar lavage from an immunocompromised patient shows clustered round to cup-shaped cysts with thick walls that stain strongly with methenamine silver and appear foamy on H&E, as seen in the photo. Which organism is shown?
A CSF culture from a patient with suspected fungal meningitis produces shiny, mucoid colonies, as shown in the photograph. Which fungal organism is shown?

A 24-year-old patient undergoing evaluation for unexplained hemolytic parameters has a peripheral blood smear reviewed. The photograph shows erythrocytes with markedly swollen morphology, consistent with osmotic water entry. Which solution is shown?

A 32-year-old patient presents with signs of dehydration. A peripheral smear prepared after mixing blood with an unidentified laboratory fluid shows erythrocytes with sharply shrunken, spiculated membranes. Which solution is shown, identified by its ability to cause erythrocytes to shrink due to osmotic water loss?

A bone marrow aspirate from a patient with severe anemia demonstrates a large erythroid precursor with deeply basophilic cytoplasm, fine reticular chromatin, and 1–2 prominent nucleoli, as shown in the image. Which erythroid precursor is shown?

A 58-year-old patient presents with anemia of unclear etiology. A peripheral smear demonstrates striking variability in erythrocyte size throughout the field, as shown in the image. Which red cell abnormality is shown?

A 45-year-old patient with chronic liver disease undergoes smear review revealing dense erythrocytes with irregularly spaced, variably sized, thorn-like projections, as shown in the image. Which red cell abnormality is shown?
A trauma patient’s peripheral smear shows a helmet-shaped cell with two sharp, horn-like projections, as illustrated in the photograph. Which red cell form is shown?

A patient with a family history of hereditary hemolytic anemia is evaluated with a peripheral smear. The photograph shows uniformly elongated, cigar-shaped erythrocytes. Which red cell abnormality is shown?
A pediatric smear shows erythrocytes with partially vacuolated, blister-like projections, some of which have collapsed into dense, shrunken remnants, as pictured. Which red cell form is shown?
A 17-year-old patient with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises has a smear reviewed showing rigid, elongated, sickle-shaped erythrocytes with pointed ends. Which red cell form is shown?
A peripheral smear from a patient with suspected membrane transport abnormalities shows erythrocytes with slit-like, mouth-shaped central pallor. Which red cell abnormality is shown?

A 47-year-old patient undergoing evaluation for chronic anemia has a peripheral blood smear reviewed. The photograph shows erythrocytes with a central area of hemoglobin, a surrounding clear zone, and an outer rim of hemoglobin, forming a bull’s-eye configuration. Which red cell form is shown, identified by its central area of hemoglobin surrounded by a clear ring and an outer rim of hemoglobin, producing a bull’s-eye appearance?

A 62-year-old patient with severe anemia undergoes a smear evaluation. The photograph demonstrates a thin, looped, reddish-violet ring within an erythrocyte, occasionally forming a figure-of-eight. Which intracytoplasmic RBC structure is shown, identified by its thin, looped or figure-of-eight reddish-violet ring composed of residual mitotic spindle material?

A 35-year-old patient with suspected oxidative hemolysis undergoes supravital staining of a peripheral smear. The photograph shows multiple round, membrane-associated inclusions. Which erythrocyte inclusion is shown, identified by round, supravital-stain–positive aggregates of denatured hemoglobin often seen in oxidative hemolysis?

A 29-year-old patient with chronic hemolytic anemia is evaluated using a peripheral smear. The photograph reveals dense, rectangular hemoglobin crystals within erythrocytes. Which intracellular RBC structure is shown, identified by dense, rectangular, bar-shaped crystalline hemoglobin aggregates formed due to β-globin substitution at position 6?

A 54-year-old patient with suspected sideroblastic changes has a smear reviewed. The photograph shows small, clustered basophilic granules near the RBC periphery. Which erythrocyte inclusion is shown, identified by small, clustered, basophilic granules composed of iron that stain positively with Prussian blue?

A 70-year-old patient with hypergammaglobulinemia presents with an erythrocyte smear showing linear stacking of red cells resembling coins. Which erythrocyte pattern is shown, identified by linear, coin-stack–like aggregation of red cells caused by increased plasma protein–mediated bridging?

A 40-year-old patient with vitamin B12 deficiency has a peripheral smear showing predominance of markedly enlarged erythrocytes. Which red cell abnormality is shown, identified by a predominance of enlarged erythrocytes with increased mean cell volume and broadened size distribution?

A 23-year-old patient with suspected G6PD deficiency presents with a smear showing cells with clean, semicircular membrane defects, as seen in the provided photograph. Which red cell abnormality is shown, identified by semicircular membrane defects produced when the spleen removes Heinz body–containing portions of oxidatively damaged erythrocytes?

A 36-year-old patient with hereditary spherocytosis has a smear reviewed showing small, densely staining erythrocytes lacking central pallor. Which erythrocyte form is shown, identified by small, densely staining red cells lacking central pallor due to membrane loss and increased surface tension?

A 52-year-old patient with suspected acute leukemia undergoes bone marrow evaluation. The photograph shows linear, needle-like azurophilic inclusions within myeloblasts. Which intracellular inclusion is shown, identified by linear or needle-shaped reddish azurophilic structures formed from fused primary granules within myeloblasts?

A 35-year-old patient presents with fever and acute bacterial infection. A peripheral blood smear is prepared, and the photograph shows a leukocyte with a multilobed nucleus connected by thin filaments and cytoplasm containing fine, neutral-staining specific granules. Which leukocyte is shown, identified by its multilobed nucleus connected by thin filaments and cytoplasm filled with fine, neutral-staining specific granules?

A 60-year-old patient with chronic inflammatory disease has a differential count performed. The photograph shows a large leukocyte with abundant slate-gray cytoplasm containing fine azurophilic granules and occasional vacuoles. The nucleus is folded and kidney-shaped without true segmentation. Which leukocyte is shown, identified by its large size, abundant slate-gray cytoplasm with fine azurophilic granules, and a folded or kidney-shaped nucleus lacking true segmentation?

A 48-year-old patient with progressive fatigue and glossitis is found to have macrocytic anemia. A peripheral smear is reviewed, and the photograph shows neutrophils with more than five nuclear lobes. Which hematologic finding is shown, characterized by a neutrophil with more than five nuclear lobes indicating impaired DNA synthesis?

A young adult with a known mucopolysaccharidosis undergoes peripheral smear examination. The photograph shows cells with large, coarse cytoplasmic inclusions, many surrounded by a clear halo, in leukocytes that can resemble macrophages. Which hematologic abnormality is shown, identified by large, coarse cytoplasmic inclusions with a surrounding clear halo in cells that resemble macrophages?

A child with hepatosplenomegaly and easy bruising undergoes bone marrow aspiration. The marrow smear photograph reveals large macrophages with abundant cytoplasm packed with blue, fibrillar inclusions that create a “wrinkled tissue paper” appearance. Which bone marrow finding is shown, identified by a macrophage containing prominent blue, fibrillar cytoplasmic inclusions with a “wrinkled tissue paper” appearance?

A 25-year-old healthy adult has a routine complete blood count and peripheral smear performed as part of an employment screen. The smear photograph shows small lymphoid cells with a dense, round nucleus occupying most of the cell and only a thin rim of deeply basophilic cytoplasm. Which hematologic cell is shown, identified by its dense, round nucleus occupying most of the cell and a thin rim of deeply basophilic cytoplasm?

A 72-year-old patient presents with lymphocytosis and fatigue. Peripheral blood smear examination reveals numerous small, mature-appearing lymphocytes with condensed chromatin and scant cytoplasm, as well as a fragile ruptured lymphocyte (smudge cell) in the photograph. Which hematologic disorder is shown, identified by numerous small to medium mature-appearing lymphocytes with the presence of a characteristic smudge cell?

A 58-year-old patient with a history of multiple myeloma undergoes bone marrow evaluation. The photograph shows a cell with an eccentrically placed nucleus, deeply basophilic cytoplasm, and a distinct pale perinuclear clearing. Which hematologic cell is shown, identified by its eccentrically placed nucleus, deeply basophilic cytoplasm, and prominent perinuclear hof?

A 63-year-old patient with a longstanding plasma cell dyscrasia has a bone marrow smear examined. The photograph demonstrates a plasma cell with an eccentric nucleus and cytoplasm packed with multiple round, homogeneous, spherical inclusions. Which hematologic cell is shown, identified by an eccentrically placed nucleus and cytoplasm packed with multiple homogeneous, spherical Russell bodies?

A 45-year-old patient presents with fatigue, bleeding, and recurrent infections. Bone marrow and peripheral blood smears are reviewed, and the photograph shows numerous blasts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, fine chromatin, and prominent nucleoli, with minimal evidence of maturation into more differentiated myeloid forms. Which leukemia subtype is shown, identified by a marrow/peripheral smear packed with myeloblasts lacking significant maturation and containing prominent nucleoli?

A 43-year-old patient presents with fatigue, bruising, and leukocytosis. Bone marrow aspirate shows sheets of blasts on the smear photograph. The blasts are medium-sized with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, fine chromatin, and no obvious granules, Auer rods, or morphologic signs of myeloid maturation. Cytochemical stains for myeloperoxidase and Sudan Black B are negative. Which leukemia subtype is shown, identified by blasts that lack morphologic evidence of maturation and require immunophenotyping to confirm myeloid lineage?

A 55-year-old patient presents with anemia, easy bruising, and leukocytosis. Bone marrow aspirate shows numerous blasts on the photograph, along with clear maturation into promyelocytes and myelocytes. Many cells contain slender, single Auer rods in their cytoplasm. Which leukemia subtype is shown, identified by myeloblasts demonstrating clear maturation beyond the blast stage and containing numerous single Auer rods?

A 49-year-old patient presents with fatigue, gingival bleeding, and splenomegaly. Bone marrow biopsy and aspirate smears, shown in the photograph, reveal increased blasts as well as a mix of granulocytic precursors and monocytic elements, including monoblasts and promonocytes. Which hematologic condition is shown, identified by marrow infiltration of both granulocytic and monocytic precursors with increased myeloblasts and monoblasts?

A child presents with fever, bone pain, and marked leukocytosis. Peripheral blood smear, as shown in the photograph, reveals small-to-medium sized blasts with condensed chromatin, scant basophilic cytoplasm, and a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Nuclear contours are somewhat irregular, but cytoplasmic granules are absent. Which hematologic finding is shown, identified by small-to-medium lymphoblasts with condensed chromatin, scant cytoplasm, and a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio in the peripheral blood smear?

A 32-year-old patient presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy, night sweats, and weight loss. Lymph node excision is performed, and the histologic section in the photograph shows giant atypical cells with abundant cytoplasm and a large bilobed nucleus, each lobe containing a prominent eosinophilic nucleolus, giving an “owl’s-eye” appearance. Which cell type is shown, identified by its large bilobed nucleus with prominent eosinophilic nucleoli giving an “owl’s-eye” appearance?

A 67-year-old patient presents with diffuse erythroderma and intense pruritus. Peripheral blood smear, as shown in the photograph, reveals circulating atypical lymphoid cells with markedly convoluted, cerebriform nuclei and a thin rim of pale cytoplasm. Which abnormal lymphoid cell is shown, identified by its cerebriform, highly convoluted nucleus and scant cytoplasm in circulating neoplastic T-helper cells?

A middle-aged patient presents with several-year history of pruritic, smudgy erythematous patches and plaques on the trunk and buttocks. A skin biopsy is performed, and the photograph shows epidermal infiltration by atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism. Clinically, the lesions are ill-defined and slowly progressive. Which cutaneous lymphoid disorder is shown, identified by smudgy, ill-defined erythematous patches and plaques typical of epidermotropic neoplastic T-cell infiltration?

A 65-year-old patient with anemia and elevated serum iron undergoes bone marrow examination. Prussian blue stain of marrow smears, shown in the photograph, demonstrates erythroid precursors whose nuclei are surrounded by a complete ring of iron-laden granules. Which abnormal erythroid finding is shown, identified by perinuclear iron-laden granules forming a complete ring around the nucleus on Prussian blue stain?

A 70-year-old patient presents with fatigue and splenomegaly. Laboratory findings reveal persistent monocytosis with a markedly elevated absolute monocyte count. Peripheral smear and bone marrow aspirate, as seen in the photograph, show increased monocytes, promonocytes, and dysplastic granulocytic precursors. Which myeloid neoplasm is shown, identified by persistent peripheral blood monocytosis with dysplastic granulocytic and monocytic precursors?

A hematology technologist is performing a manual reticulocyte count using supravital-stained blood. Under the microscope, the photograph shows a special eyepiece reticle with two unequal squares: a large square used to count reticulocytes and a smaller square used to count red blood cells in the same field. Which laboratory measurement tool is shown, identified by a reticle containing a large square used for reticulocyte counting and a smaller square used for erythrocyte enumeration in the same field?

A 29-year-old patient with allergic rhinitis undergoes a complete blood count due to persistent eosinophilia. A peripheral smear is prepared, and the photograph shows a leukocyte with a distinctly bilobed nucleus and large, uniform, refractile orange-red cytoplasmic granules. Which leukocyte is shown, identified by a bilobed nucleus and large refractile orange-red cytoplasmic granules on Wright–Giemsa stain?

A 44-year-old patient with chronic urticaria undergoes a CBC. The peripheral smear photograph shows a circulating granulocyte whose nucleus is partially obscured by numerous large, dark blue-black granules. Which leukocyte is shown, identified by its lobulated nucleus obscured by dense, dark blue-black granules rich in histamine and heparin?

A 17-year-old patient undergoing evaluation for anemia has blood drawn into several collection tubes. The lavender-top tube in the photograph is used for hematologic testing. Which anticoagulant is used, identified by its lavender (purple) top tube containing a calcium-chelating agent for hematology testing?

A 50-year-old patient with suspected coagulopathy has blood drawn for clot-based assays. The photograph shows a light-blue–stoppered tube used for PT, APTT, and factor studies. Which coagulation tube is shown, identified by its light-blue stopper requiring a precise anticoagulant-to-blood ratio to ensure valid clot-based testing?

A 38-year-old patient undergoing metabolic testing has blood collected into a green-top tube as shown in the photograph. Which anticoagulant is used, identified by its green-stoppered tube containing an agent that inhibits coagulation by accelerating antithrombin activity?
